Unlike prior work that relies on dense sensor fusion or geometric projections, our approach learns latent representations that preserve only state transitions critical for value-based planning. This reduces computational overhead while maintaining closed-loop driving performance. We validate the method on CARLA benchmarks by comparing driving scores, collision rates, and inference speed against geometry-based fusion baselines.

The compact latent space enables fast planning with a lightweight value network.

hypothesis.title: Pseudo-Simulation for Closed-Loop Evaluation of Value-Equivalent Driving Policies
hypothesis.summary: We extend pseudo-simulation by incorporating value-equivalent model predictions to evaluate end-to-end driving policies under compounding errors. Unlike open-loop metrics that ignore agent-environment interactions, our method generates synthetic observations weighted by proximity to value-equivalent state transitions. This enables closed-loop-like assessment of policies trained with value-equivalent representations, bridging the gap between open/closed-loop evaluation.
hypothesis.gap: Pseudo-simulation improves open-loop evaluation realism but still lacks dynamic agent interactions. Value-equivalent models enable efficient planning but are untested under compounding error conditions typical of closed-loop driving.
hypothesis.approach: We modify pseudo-simulation's weighting scheme to prioritize synthetic observations matching value-equivalent state transitions. A value-equivalent model predicts future states for each candidate action, and synthetic observations are weighted by Bellman error. This creates a simulated environment where policies are tested on trajectories that preserve value-relevant dynamics.
hypothesis.evaluation: We compare correlation coefficients (R²) between pseudo-simulation metrics and true closed-loop performance (CARLA Leaderboard) for value-equivalent vs. geometry-based policies. Additional metrics include collision recovery rate and route completion under adversarial traffic. Success requires R² > 0.85 and matching closed-loop ranking.

refined.title: Value-Equivalent Weighting for Pseudo-Simulation in Autonomous Driving
refined.summary: We integrate value-equivalent model predictions into pseudo-simulation to better approximate closed-loop evaluation of driving policies. By weighting synthetic observations based on Bellman error between predicted and actual state transitions, our method prioritizes trajectories that preserve value-relevant dynamics. This bridges the gap between open-loop evaluation and closed-loop performance for policies trained with value-equivalent representations.

refined.evaluation: We compare correlation (R²) between pseudo-simulation metrics and closed-loop performance (CARLA Leaderboard) for value-equivalent vs. proximity-weighted pseudo-simulation. We use the NAVSIM dataset (ref-020) with adversarial traffic scenarios from ref-034, reporting collision recovery rate (percentage of collisions avoided after 5s) and route completion. An ablation isolates value-equivalent weighting by comparing against pseudo-simulation with ref-010's proximity weighting.

hypothesis.title: Proxy Reward Unhackability in End-to-End Driving via Multi-Objective Optimization
hypothesis.summary: We formalize and measure reward hacking in end-to-end driving by training policies on misspecified proxy rewards while monitoring true reward performance. We propose a multi-objective optimization framework that explicitly penalizes divergence between proxy and true reward gradients, demonstrating reduced hacking on CARLA's NoCrash benchmark through phase transition detection and anomaly scoring.
hypothesis.gap: While reward hacking is documented (ref-008, ref-016), no work systematically measures its emergence or proposes mitigation strategies for end-to-end driving. Existing solutions focus on static proxy design rather than dynamic optimization.
hypothesis.approach: We extend the unhackability framework (ref-016) by integrating gradient alignment constraints into PPO training. The policy is optimized not only for proxy reward but also to minimize the angle between proxy and true reward gradients, detected via auxiliary critics.
hypothesis.evaluation: We measure hacking via true reward drop thresholds and phase transition points on CARLA's NoCrash scenarios. Baselines include standard PPO (ref-005) and static proxy designs (ref-016), with success defined by maintaining >90% true reward despite proxy misspecification.

hypothesis.title: World-on-Rails Imitation with Value-Equivalent Dynamics

The approach ensures the non-reactive simulation retains sufficient causal structure for effective policy training, bridging the gap between open-loop data and closed-loop control.

hypothesis.title: Reward-Gaming Detection via Value-Equivalent Model Discrepancy
hypothesis.summary: We detect reward hacking in end-to-end driving policies by measuring discrepancies between value-equivalent model predictions and actual policy behavior. Unlike reward shaping or anomaly detection, our method identifies reward gaming through inconsistencies in the policy's internal value model, which should align with the true environment dynamics under an unhackable proxy.

Discrepancies exceeding a threshold (learned from safe trajectories) trigger alerts. The model is updated via online inverse dynamics learning to adapt to new scenarios.
hypothesis.evaluation: We test on CARLA environments with misspecified rewards (e.g., ignoring traffic rules). Metrics include false positive rate, detection delay, and collision prevention rate. We compare against reward anomaly detection baselines. Success requires >90% true positive rate with <5% false positives in adversarial scenarios.
